zajjaj:38-38.t:
And His saying: ﴿يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾. It is also read "جاءانا" (the two of them came to Us). Whoever reads "جاءانا", the meaning is: "until, when the disbeliever and his devil came…"; and whoever reads "حَتّى إذا جاءَنا" (until, when he came to Us), it refers to the disbeliever alone. ﴿قالَ يا لَيْتَ بَيْنِي وبَيْنَكَ بُعْدَ المَشْرِقَيْنِ فَبِئْسَ القَرِينُ﴾: the meaning of "اَلْمَشْرِقَيْنِ" (the two easts) here is the distance between the east and the west; when they were made a pair, the word "east" prevailed (taghlīb), as the poet said:
لَنا قَمَراها والنُّجُومُ الطَّوالِعُ
(Ours are its two moons and the rising stars.)
He means the sun and the moon; and as they said: "سُنَّةُ العُمَرَيْنِ" (the practice of the two ʿUmars), meaning the practice of Abū Bakr and ʿUmar, may Allah have mercy on them both.

zajjaj:39-39.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَنْ يَنْفَعَكُمُ اليَوْمَ إذْ ظَلَمْتُمْ أنَّكم في العَذابِ مُشْتَرِكُونَ﴾: the meaning is: "Sharing in the punishment will not benefit you." Muḥammad ibn Yazīd [al-Mubarrad] said, in answer concerning this verse: They were denied the relief of consolation (al-taʾassī), because consolation makes calamity easier to bear; so they were informed that sharing in the punishment would not benefit them, and that Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, would place no consolation in it. He said: And he recited to me on this meaning, by al-Khansāʾ:
وَلَوْلا كَثْرَةُ الباكِينَ حَوْلِي ∗∗∗ عَلى إخْوانِهِمْ لَقَتَلْتُ نَفْسِي
(Were it not for the many around me weeping over their brothers, I would have killed myself.)

وَما يَبْكُونَ مِثْلَ أخِي ولَكِنْ ∗∗∗ أُعَزِّي النَّفْسَ عَنْهُ بِالتَّأسِّي
(They do not weep for one like my brother, but I console my soul over him by taking comfort in others' grief.)

zajjaj:41-41.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإمّا نَذْهَبَنَّ بِكَ فَإنّا مِنهم مُنْتَقِمُونَ﴾ ﴿أوْ نُرِيَنَّكَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 42]: "ما" entered as an emphasis (tawkīd) of the condition, and the heavy nūn in His saying ﴿نَذْهَبَنَّ﴾ also entered as emphasis. When "ما" enters, the nūn enters with it, just as it enters together with the lām of the oath. The meaning is: "We shall take vengeance on them if you are taken in death, or We shall show you what We promised them, and what We promised you concerning them, of victory." And Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, did indeed show him what He promised him concerning them, and what He promised them, of their destruction if they denied. It has also been said: there were things after the Messenger of Allah ﷺ which Allah did not wish to show him.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَإنَّهُ لَذِكْرٌ لَكَ ولِقَوْمِكَ﴾: He means that the Qur'an is an honour for you and for your people.
And His saying: ﴿وَسَوْفَ تُسْألُونَ﴾: its meaning is: you will be asked about giving thanks for the honour Allah has granted you.

zajjaj:45-45.t:
And His saying: ﴿واسْألْ مَن أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ مِن رُسُلِنا أجَعَلْنا مِن دُونِ الرَّحْمَنِ آلِهَةً يُعْبَدُونَ﴾: there are three aspects (awjuh) to this question. It has come in the exegesis «that on the night the Prophet ﷺ was taken on the Night Journey, the prophets were gathered for him in Jerusalem (Bayt al-Maqdis), and he led them and prayed with them; and it was said to him: Ask them; but he, peace be upon him, did not doubt and did not ask».
A second aspect, which is the one I choose, is that the meaning is: "Ask the nations of those of Our messengers whom We sent before you: did We appoint gods besides the All-Merciful to be worshipped?" The meaning of the question here is by way of eliciting acknowledgement (taqrīr), as He said: ﴿وَلَئِنْ سَألْتَهم مَن خَلَقَهم لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 87]; He does not ask them here about who created them except by way of taqrīr. Likewise, if he asked all the nations of the prophets, they would not produce [evidence] that in their books is "Worship other than Me." A third aspect: the meaning, in the address to the Prophet ﷺ, is an address to the community, as though He said: "And ask (plural)." The proof that the community may be included in an address to the Prophet ﷺ is His saying: ﴿يا أيُّها النَّبِيُّ إذا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّساءَ﴾ [al-Ṭalāq: 1].

zajjaj:49-49.t: And His saying: ﴿وَقالُوا يا أيُّهَ السّاحِرُ ادْعُ لَنا رَبَّكَ بِما عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ إنَّنا لَمُهْتَدُونَ﴾: If someone asks: How could they say to Moses, peace be upon him, "O sorcerer," while they claim that they will be rightly guided? The answer is that they addressed him with the name of sorcery by which he had previously been called among them. The meaning of "بِما عَهِدَ عِنْدَكَ" is: "by what He has covenanted with you concerning whoever believes in Him, namely the removal of the punishment from him." The proof of that is His saying: ﴿فَلَمّا كَشَفْنا عَنْهُمُ العَذابَ إذا هم يَنْكُثُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 50], that is: then they broke their covenant.

zajjaj:51-51.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنادى فِرْعَوْنُ في قَوْمِهِ قالَ يا قَوْمِ ألَيْسَ لِي مُلْكُ مِصْرَ وهَذِهِ الأنْهارُ تَجْرِي مِن تَحْتِي﴾: "مِصْرَ" here means the well-known city of Miṣr. Miṣr is a masculine [word] used as the name of something feminine, because femininity predominates for "city" (madīna). "مُلْكُ مِصْرٍ" (with tanwīn) is also permissible, taking Miṣr as the name of a country (balad); but this is far-fetched, because "balad" is mostly used for what contains large cities, such as the lands of the Byzantines (bilād al-Rūm), the lands of Syria (bilād al-Shām) and the country of Khurāsān. It is permissible to make Miṣr fully declinable (taṣrif), i.e. not treat it as a diptote, when you make it the name of a country, according to all the grammarians among the Basrans.

zajjaj:52-52.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 51] ﴿أمْ أنا خَيْرٌ مِن هَذا الَّذِي هو مَهِينٌ﴾: Sībawayh and al-Khalīl said: "أنا" is conjoined by "أمْ" to His saying "أفَلا تُبْصِرُونَ", because the meaning of "أمْ أنا خَيْرٌ" is "or do you see?", as though he said: "Do you not see, or do you see?!" He said: because if they said, "You are better than him," they would have become, in his view, people who see; so it is as though he said: "Do you not see, or are you people who see?!" The meaning of "مَهِينٌ" is: paltry; one says "شَيْءٌ مَهِينٌ", that is, a paltry thing; it is on the pattern "فَعِيلٌ", from "اَلْمَهانَةِ" (contemptibility).
And His saying: ﴿وَلا يَكادُ يُبِينُ﴾: he said that because there was a lisp (luthgha) in the tongue of Moses, peace be upon him; and the prophets, Allah's blessings be upon them all, are clear in speech and eloquent.

zajjaj:53-53.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَوْلا أُلْقِيَ عَلَيْهِ أسْوِرَةٌ مِن ذَهَبٍ أوْ جاءَ مَعَهُ المَلائِكَةُ مُقْتَرِنِينَ﴾: It is as though, when he had described himself as having kingship and leadership, he said: Why did Moses not bring something to be cast upon him, which would be bracelets of gold, showing that they are from his God to whose oneness he calls you; or why did the angels not come with him, accompanying (muqtarinīn), that is, walking with him and showing the soundness of his prophethood? Moses, peace be upon him, had brought signs containing proof establishing his prophethood, and those to whom the prophets are sent have no right to propose whatever signs they themselves want. It is also read: "أساوِرَةٌ مِن ذَهَبٍ". It may be a plural of a plural: you say "أسْوِرَةٌ" and "أساوِرَةٌ", as you say "أقْوالٌ" and "أقاوِيلُ". It may also be the plural of "إسْوارٌ", giving "أساوِرَةٌ".
"أساوِرَةٌ" was made declinable (ṣurifat) only because you joined the hāʾ to "أساوِرَ", so it became one noun, and the noun came to have a pattern matching the singular, like "عَلانِيَةٌ" and "عَباقِيَةٌ".

zajjaj:55-55.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَلَمّا آسَفُونا انْتَقَمْنا مِنهُمْ﴾: the meaning of "آسَفُونا" is: they angered Us.

zajjaj:56-56.t: ﴿فَجَعَلْناهم سَلَفًا ومَثَلا لِلآخِرِينَ﴾: We made them a precedent (salaf), gone before, so that those after might take warning from them. It is also read "سُلُفًا", with ḍamma on the sīn and the lām, and it is read "سُلَفًا", with ḍamma on the sīn and fatḥa on the lām. Whoever says "سُلُفًا" with two ḍammas, it is the plural of "سَلِيفٌ", that is, a whole group that has passed; and whoever reads "سُلَفًا", it is the plural of "سُلْفَةٌ", that is, a party that has passed.

zajjaj:57-57.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمّا ضُرِبَ ابْنُ مَرْيَمَ مَثَلا إذا قَوْمُكَ مِنهُ يَصِدُّونَ﴾: It is also read "يَصُدُّونَ", with ḍamma on the ṣād, but the kasra is more common. The meaning of both is: "they clamour"; and it is possible that the meaning of the one with ḍamma is "they turn away." It has come in the exegesis that the disbelievers of Quraysh disputed with the Prophet ﷺ: when it was said to them, ﴿إنَّكم وما تَعْبُدُونَ مِن دُونِ اللَّهِ حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ﴾ [al-Anbiyāʾ: 98], they said: We are content for our gods to be in the position of Jesus son of Mary and the angels, who were worshipped besides Allah. This is the meaning of Jesus being cited as an example.

zajjaj:58-58.t:
And His saying: ﴿ما ضَرَبُوهُ لَكَ إلا جَدَلا﴾: that is, seeking dispute, because they knew that the meaning of "حَصَبُ جَهَنَّمَ" here is that He meant by it the idols, and they.
«[Translator's note: the source text ends abruptly with "وهم" (and they); the sentence appears to be incomplete.]»

zajjaj:59-59.t: And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿إنْ هو إلا عَبْدٌ أنْعَمْنا عَلَيْهِ وجَعَلْناهُ مَثَلا لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ﴾: He means by it Jesus son of Mary. The meaning of "وَجَعَلْناهُ مَثَلًا لِبَنِي إسْرائِيلَ" is that he points them to his prophethood.

zajjaj:60-60.t:
﴿وَلَوْ نَشاءُ لَجَعَلْنا مِنكم مَلائِكَةً في الأرْضِ يَخْلُفُونَ﴾: the meaning of "يَخْلُفُونَ" is: some of them succeed others. And the meaning is: "We would have made from them a replacement for you."
«[Translator's note: the source reads "مِنهم" (from them) in this paraphrase, whereas the verse has "مِنكم" (from you).]»

zajjaj:61-61.t:
﴿وَإنَّهُ لَعِلْمٌ لِلسّاعَةِ﴾: It is also read "لَعَلَمٌ لِلسّاعَةِ" (a sign of the Hour). The meaning is that the appearance of Jesus son of Mary, peace be upon him, is a sign of the Hour, that is, when he appears it indicates the coming of the Hour. It has also been said that He means by it that the Qur'an is the sign of the Hour, indicating the nearness of its coming; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿اقْتَرَبَتِ السّاعَةُ وانْشَقَّ القَمَرُ﴾ [al-Qamar: 1]. The first is more common in the exegesis.
And His saying: ﴿فَلا تَمْتَرُنَّ بِها﴾, that is: do not doubt it at all.

zajjaj:63-63.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَمّا جاءَ عِيسى بِالبَيِّناتِ قالَ قَدْ جِئْتُكم بِالحِكْمَةِ ولأُبَيِّنَ لَكم بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ﴾: His saying "جاءَ بِالحِكْمَةِ", that is, with the Gospel; and "بِالبَيِّناتِ", that is, the signs which created beings are incapable of [producing]. They said concerning the meaning of "بَعْضَ الَّذِي تَخْتَلِفُونَ فِيهِ": that is, all that they differ about; and they cited as evidence the saying of Labīd:
أوْ تَخْتَرِمْ بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حِمامُها
(Or its fated death carries off some souls.)
He means all souls. They also cited the saying of al-Quṭāmī:
قَدْ يُدْرِكُ المُتَأنِّي بَعْضَ حاجَتِهِ
(The patient one may attain some of his need.)
They said: its meaning is "all of his need." This is the view of Abū ʿUbayda. The correct view is that "some" (al-baʿḍ) does not have the meaning of "all" (al-kull), and this does not occur in the language. What Jesus brought in the Gospel was only some of what they differed about, and Allah, Glorified is He, made clear to them, apart from the Gospel, what they needed. Likewise his saying:
أوْ تَخْتَرِمْ بَعْضَ النُّفُوسِ حِمامُها
He means only his own soul, and his soul is some of the souls.

zajjaj:65-65.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فاخْتَلَفَ الأحْزابُ مِن بَيْنِهِمْ﴾: "اَلْأحْزابُ" (the factions): it has been said that they are the four who came after Jesus; He means by it the Jews and the Christians.
And His saying: ﴿الأخِلاءُ يَوْمَئِذٍ بَعْضُهم لِبَعْضٍ عَدُوٌّ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 67]: It has come in the exegesis from the Prophet ﷺ that he said: «"Close friends are four: two believers and two disbelievers. One of the two believers dies and is asked about his close friend, and he says: I knew him only as one who constantly enjoined what is right and constantly forbade what is wrong; O Allah, guide him as You guided me, and cause him to die upon what You caused me to die upon. And the disbeliever is asked about his close friend, and he says: I knew him only as one who constantly enjoined what is wrong and constantly forbade what is right; O Allah, lead him astray as You led me astray, and cause him to die upon what You caused me to die upon. Then, when the Day of Resurrection comes, each one speaks ill of his companion."»

zajjaj:68-68.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿يا عِبادِ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ اليَوْمَ ولا أنْتُمْ تَحْزَنُونَ﴾: It is also read "يا عِبادِي", with the yāʾ retained. We have explained the omission and retention of the yāʾ in cases like this earlier in the book.

zajjaj:69-69.t: And His saying: ﴿الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا بِآياتِنا وكانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ﴾: "اَلَّذِينَ" is in the position of the accusative (naṣb) as a naʿt (adjective) of "عِبادِي", because "عِبادِي" is a muḍāf vocative (munādā). "لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمُ اليَوْمَ" was said only to the believers, not to others; and likewise ﴿ادْخُلُوا الجَنَّةَ لا خَوْفٌ عَلَيْكُمْ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 49], meaning: "O My believing servants, enter Paradise."

zajjaj:70-70.t: And His saying: ﴿أنْتُمْ وأزْواجُكم تُحْبَرُونَ﴾: "تُحْبَرُونَ": you will be honoured with an honour carried to the utmost. And "اَلْحَبْرَةُ" is going to the utmost in what is described as beautiful.

zajjaj:71-71.t:
And His saying: ﴿يُطافُ عَلَيْهِمْ بِصِحافٍ مِن ذَهَبٍ وأكْوابٍ﴾: "اَلصِّحافُ": its singular is "صَحْفَةٌ", which is a large bowl (qaṣʿa). And "الأكْوابُ": its singular is "كُوبٌ", which is a round vessel without a handle.
And His saying: ﴿وَفِيها ما تَشْتَهِيهِ الأنْفُسُ﴾: it has been read "تَشْتَهِيهِ الأنْفُسُ" with the hāʾ retained; most of the codices (maṣāḥif) are without it, and in some of them is the hāʾ.

zajjaj:75-75.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لا يُفَتَّرُ عَنْهم وهم فِيهِ مُبْلِسُونَ﴾: "اَلْمُبْلِسُ" is the one who is silent and holds back, as one despairing of relief holds back.

zajjaj:76-76.t: And His saying: ﴿وَلَكِنْ كانُوا هُمُ الظّالِمِينَ﴾: "هم" here is a separating pronoun (faṣl); this is what the Basrans call it. It comes as an indication that what follows it is not an adjective of what precedes it, and that the speaker is bringing the predicate (khabar) of the first. The Kufans call it "اَلْعِمادَ" (the support). According to the Basrans it has no position in the nominative, the accusative or the genitive, and they claim that it is in the same position as "ما" in His saying, Glorified is He: ﴿فَبِما رَحْمَةٍ مِنَ اللَّهِ لِنْتَ لَهُمْ﴾ [Āl ʿImrān: 159]; "ما" in this has been explained earlier in the book. "وَلَكِنْ كانُوا هُمُ الظّالِمُونَ" is permissible outside the Qur'an, but do not ever read it so, because it contradicts the codex (al-muṣḥaf).

zajjaj:77-77.t:
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَنادَوْا يا مالِكُ لِيَقْضِ عَلَيْنا رَبُّكَ﴾: It has been transmitted as "يا مالِ", without the kāf and with kasra on the lām. The grammarians call this "اَلتَّرْخِيمَ" (tarkhīm, vocative truncation). It is frequent in poetry in "مالِكٌ" and "عامِرٌ", but I dislike them both [here], because they contradict the codex.
«[Translator's note: "them both" presumably refers to the two truncated forms (e.g. "يا مالِ" with kasra and its variant); the source does not specify.]»

zajjaj:79-79.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أمْ أبْرَمُوا أمْرًا فَإنّا مُبْرِمُونَ﴾: that is, or have they firmly settled, in their own minds, some matter of plotting or evil? Then We are settling firmly, making firm their requital: plotting for their plotting and evil for their evil.

zajjaj:81-81.t: And His saying: ﴿قُلْ إنْ كانَ لِلرَّحْمَنِ ولَدٌ فَأنا أوَّلُ العابِدِينَ﴾: its meaning is: "If you claim that the All-Merciful has a son, then I am the first of those who affirm His oneness," because whoever worships Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, and acknowledges that He is his God, has rejected that He should have a son. The meaning is: "If the All-Merciful has a son, according to what you say," as He said: ﴿أيْنَ شُرَكائِيَ الَّذِينَ كُنْتُمْ تُشاقُّونَ فِيهِمْ﴾ [al-Naḥl: 27], that is, "according to what you say"; and Allah is One, He has no partner. It has also been said that "إنْ" in this place is in the position of "ما" (negation), the meaning being: "The All-Merciful has no son, and I am the first of the worshippers." And it has been said that "اَلْعابِدِينَ" has the meaning of "اَلْآنِفِينَ" (those who disdain): "I am the first to disdain this saying."

zajjaj:84-84.t: And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَهُوَ الَّذِي في السَّماءِ إلَهٌ وفي الأرْضِ إلَهٌ﴾: the meaning is: "He is the One whose oneness is affirmed in the heaven and in the earth." It has also been read: "في السَّماءِ اللَّهُ وفي الأرْضِ اللَّهُ". What He created between them and in them shows that He is One, Wise, Knowing, because their creation indicates wisdom and knowledge.

zajjaj:88-88.t:
And His saying: ﴿وَقِيلِهِ يا رَبِّ إنَّ هَؤُلاءِ قَوْمٌ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾: It is also read "وَقِيلَهُ" and "قِيلُهُ يا رَبِّ". There are three aspects in it: the genitive (khafḍ), with the meaning: "And with Him is knowledge of the Hour and knowledge of his saying: O my Lord." And the accusative, from three aspects. Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said: it is accusative from two directions: one of them by conjunction with His saying "أمْ يَحْسَبُونَ أنّا لا نَسْمَعُ سِرَّهم ونَجْواهم وقِيلَهُ", that is, "and We hear his saying"; and it may be on [the pattern] "وَقالَ قِيلَهُ" (and he said his saying). Abū Isḥāq [al-Zajjāj] said: What I myself choose is that "قِيلَهُ" be accusative with the meaning: "And with Him is knowledge of the Hour, and He knows his saying," so the meaning would be: "He knows the unseen and knows his saying," because the meaning of "عِنْدَهُ عِلْمُ السّاعَةِ" is "He knows the Hour and knows his saying." The meaning of "اَلسّاعَةُ" throughout the Qur'an is the time at which the Resurrection takes place. And the nominative is with the meaning: "And his saying is this saying," that is: "And his saying is his words: O my Lord, these are a people who do not believe."
«[Translator's note: the source says "three aspects" for the accusative but explicitly lists al-Akhfash's two and al-Zajjāj's own preferred one, which together make three.]»

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Zukhruf
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿حم﴾ ﴿والكِتابِ المُبِينِ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 2] — we have already explained the meaning of "Ḥā Mīm". The meaning of "الكِتابِ المُبِينِ" (the clear Book) is: the one that has made the ways of guidance distinct from the ways of misguidance, and has made clear everything that the community needs.

zajjaj:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكم فِيها سُبُلا﴾: roads.

zajjaj:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿والَّذِي خَلَقَ الأزْواجَ كُلَّها﴾ — its meaning is: He created all the kinds. You say: "عِنْدِي مِن كُلِّ زَوْجٍ" (I have some of every zawj), that is: of every kind. ﴿وَجَعَلَ لَكم مِنَ الفُلْكِ والأنْعامِ ما تَرْكَبُونَ﴾, that is: He created for you and subjected them to you, ﴿لِتَسْتَوُوا عَلى ظُهُورِهِ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13].
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ثُمَّ تَذْكُرُوا نِعْمَةَ رَبِّكم إذا اسْتَوَيْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ وتَقُولُوا سُبْحانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنا هَذا﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 13], that is: you praise Allah and magnify Him. So one says, when boarding a ship: "In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring", and says, when mounting a riding animal: "Praise be to Allah; glory be to Him who has subjected this to us, and we were not مُقْرِنِين for it", that is: "able [to manage it]". Its derivation is from your saying "أنا لِفُلانٍ مُقْرِنٌ" (I am a match for so-and-so), that is: able to cope with him, that is: I have become an equal (قِرْن) to him.

zajjaj:14-14.t: ﴿وَإنّا إلى رَبِّنا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ﴾, that is: we affirm the resurrection.

zajjaj:15-15.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا لَهُ مِن عِبادِهِ جُزْءًا إنَّ الإنْسانَ لَكَفُورٌ﴾ — those who made the angels the daughters of Allah are meant by it. Some of the lexicographers recited to me a verse which indicates that the meaning of "جُزْءًا" is the meaning of "females", and I do not know whether the verse is old or fabricated. He recited to me:
إنْ أجْزَأتْ حُرَّةٌ يَوْمًا فَلا عَجَبٌ ∗∗∗ قَدْ تُجْزِئُ الحُرَّةُ المِذْكارَ أحْيانا
(If a free woman one day bore a girl, it is no wonder; a free woman who usually bears sons sometimes bears a girl.)
That is: if she "bore females", gave birth to a female.

zajjaj:18-18.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أوَمَن يُنَشَّأُ في الحِلْيَةِ﴾ — and it is read "يُنْشَأُ". The position of "مَن" is accusative; the meaning is: "Have they assigned to Allah one who is brought up in ornaments — meaning daughters?!" ﴿وَهُوَ في الخِصامِ غَيْرُ مُبِينٍ﴾ — daughters are meant, that is: the female hardly makes her argument in full, nor states it clearly. It has been said in the commentary: "A woman hardly argues with a proof without it turning against her." And it has been said that He means by it the idols, but the better is that He means by it the female.

zajjaj:19-19.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَعَلُوا المَلائِكَةَ الَّذِينَ هم عِبادُ الرَّحْمَنِ إناثًا﴾ — "making" (الجَعْل) here is in the sense of saying and judging something to be so. You say: "قَدْ جَعَلْتُ زَيْدًا أعْلَمَ النّاسِ" (I have made Zayd the most learned of people), that is: "you have described him as such and judged him so".
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَتُكْتَبُ شَهادَتُهُمْ﴾ — and it is read "سَنَكْتُبُ" (We will write). "سَيَكْتُبُ" is also permissible, the meaning being: "Allah will write their testimony", but we know of no one who read it so; the reading is with tāʾ and with nūn.

zajjaj:20-20.t: His saying: ﴿وَقالُوا لَوْ شاءَ الرَّحْمَنُ ما عَبَدْناهم ما لَهم بِذَلِكَ مِن عِلْمٍ﴾ — the meaning is: "they have no knowledge for their saying that the angels are the daughters of Allah, nor for all that they conjectured".

zajjaj:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿أمْ آتَيْناهم كِتابًا مِن قَبْلِهِ﴾, that is: "or have they spoken on the basis of a book...?!" The meaning is: "Did they witness their creation, or did We bring them a book for what they said about their worship of what they worship besides Allah?!" Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that what they did was following the misguidance of their fathers, saying: ﴿بَلْ قالُوا إنّا وجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ وإنّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُهْتَدُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 22]. And it is read "عَلى إمَّةٍ" with kasra, and the meaning is: "upon a way".

zajjaj:23-23.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَكَذَلِكَ ما أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ في قَرْيَةٍ مِن نَذِيرٍ إلا قالَ مُتْرَفُوها إنّا وجَدْنا آباءَنا عَلى أُمَّةٍ﴾, that is: these have said to you just as their likes said to the messengers before you.
And His saying: ﴿وَإنّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ مُقْتَدُونَ﴾ — its meaning is: "we follow their example". It is valid for it to be a khabar (predicate) of "إنّا", [as in] "مُهْتَدُونَ", with "عَلى" being part of the complement (ṣila) of "مُهْتَدِين", and likewise "مُقْتَدُونَ", so that the meaning would be: "and they are guided upon their traces", and likewise the meaning would be: "following upon their traces". It is also valid for it to be a khabar after a khabar, so that "وَإنّا عَلى آثارِهِمْ" is the khabar and "مُهْتَدُونَ" is a second khabar, and likewise "مُقْتَدُونَ". [Translator's note: the text reads «خَبَرًا لِـ "إنّا مُهْتَدُونَ"»; the sense is that «مُهْتَدُونَ» / «مُقْتَدُونَ» is the khabar of «إنّا» with «عَلى آثارِهِمْ» attached to it.]

zajjaj:24-24.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قالَ أوَلَوْ جِئْتُكم بِأهْدى مِمّا وجَدْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ آباءَكُمْ﴾ — the meaning in it is: "Say: Will you follow what you found your fathers upon, even if I have brought you something better guided than it?!"

zajjaj:26-26.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإذْ قالَ إبْراهِيمُ لأبِيهِ وقَوْمِهِ إنَّنِي بَراءٌ مِمّا تَعْبُدُونَ﴾ ﴿إلا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 27] — "بَراءٌ" is in the sense of "بَرِيءٌ مِمّا تَعْبُدُونَ" (free of what you worship). The Arabs say, for one person: "أنا البَراءُ مِنكَ" (I am quit of you), and likewise for two, for a group, for the masculine and the feminine; they say: "نَحْنُ البَراءُ مِنكَ، والخَلاءُ مِنكَ" (we are quit of you, free of you), and they do not say "نَحْنُ البَراءانِ مِنكَ" or "البَراؤُونَ". The meaning is only: "we are possessors of quittance from you", and "we are possessors of quittance from you" [Translator's note: the source gives «إنّا ذَوُو البَراءِ مِنكَ» and «نَحْنُ ذَوُو البَراءِ مِنكَ», which mean the same], just as you say "رَجُلٌ عَدْلٌ" (a just man), "اِمْرَأةٌ عَدْلٌ" (a just woman) and "قَوْمٌ عَدْلٌ" (just people), the meaning being "possessors of justice" (ذَوُو عَدْلٍ, ذَواتُ عَدْلٍ). [Translator's note: this is a maṣdar used as a description, which does not inflect for number or gender.]

zajjaj:27-27.t: His saying: ﴿إلا الَّذِي فَطَرَنِي﴾ — the meaning is: "we declare ourselves quit of what you worship except of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He". It is also permissible that "إلّا" be in the sense of "لَكِنْ" (but), so that the meaning would be: "but the One who created me — He will guide me".

zajjaj:28-28.t: ﴿وَجَعَلَها كَلِمَةً باقِيَةً في عَقِبِهِ﴾ — He means by it the word of tawḥīd, which is "There is no god but Allah", remaining among the posterity of Ibrāhīm: there will always be among his offspring someone who affirms the oneness of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إنّا جَعَلْناهُ قُرْآنًا عَرَبِيًّا﴾ — its meaning is: "We have made it clear as an Arabic Quran".

zajjaj:31-31.t: ﴿وَقالُوا لَوْلا نُـزِّلَ هَذا القُرْآنُ عَلى رَجُلٍ مِنَ القَرْيَتَيْنِ عَظِيمٍ﴾ — the meaning is: "upon a great man of the two men of the two towns". Of the two men, one is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī, of the people of Mecca, and the other is Ḥabīb ibn ʿAmr ibn ʿUmayr al-Thaqafī, of the people of al-Ṭāʾif; and the two towns here are Mecca and al-Ṭāʾif. "لَوْلا نَزَّلَ" is permissible, that is: "why did Allah not send down this Quran", and "لَوْلا نَزَلَ هَذا القُرْآنُ" is permissible; the meaning of "لَوْلا" is "هَلّا" (why not). These latter two were not read; the reading is only "نُزِّلَ". "هَذا" is in the position of the nominative, and "القُرْآنُ" here explains "هَذا"; Sībawayh calls it "ʿaṭf al-bayān" (explicative apposition), because its form is the form of an attribute. Among what shows that it is ʿaṭf bayān is your saying: "مَرَرْتُ بِهَذا الرَّجُلِ" (I passed by this man), "بِهَذِهِ الدّارِ" (by this house), and "هَذا القُرْآنُ" (this Quran): after "هَذا" one mentions only a noun by which one explains the demonstrative.

zajjaj:32-32.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿أهم يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ﴾, that is: their saying "Why was this Quran not sent down upon someone other than Muḥammad, peace be upon him?" is an objection on their part, and the bounty of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, is not apportioned by anyone other than Him. When the Prophet ﷺ came with the message, the Arabs — or most of them — said: "How is it that Allah did not send an angel?! How is it that Allah sent a human?!" So Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿وَما أرْسَلْنا مِن قَبْلِكَ إلا رِجالا نُوحِي إلَيْهِمْ مِن أهْلِ القُرى﴾ [Yūsuf: 109], and He said: ﴿أكانَ لِلنّاسِ عَجَبًا أنْ أوْحَيْنا إلى رَجُلٍ مِنهُمْ﴾ [Yūnus: 2]. When they heard that the message had been among men of the people of the towns, they said: "Why was it not sent down upon one of these two men?" And He, Mighty and Majestic is He, said: ﴿أهم يَقْسِمُونَ رَحْمَتَ رَبِّكَ نَحْنُ قَسَمْنا بَيْنَهم مَعِيشَتَهم في الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا ورَفَعْنا بَعْضَهم فَوْقَ بَعْضٍ دَرَجاتٍ﴾: just as We have favoured some of them over others in provision and in rank, so too We choose for the message whom We will.
And His saying: ﴿لِيَتَّخِذَ بَعْضُهم بَعْضًا سُخْرِيًّا﴾ — and "سِخْرِيًّا" — that is: so that some of them may employ others and some of them may make use of the service of others. It was also said: "سِخْرِيًّا", that is: some of them take others as slaves. Then He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that the Hereafter is a better share than this world, saying: ﴿وَرَحْمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيْرٌ مِمّا يَجْمَعُونَ﴾.

zajjaj:33-33.t:
And He made known how little this world is in His sight, Mighty and Majestic is He, saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا أنْ يَكُونَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً لَجَعَلْنا لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ سُقُفًا مِن فِضَّةٍ﴾ — and it is read "سَقْفًا مِن فِضَّةٍ", and "سُقْفًا", with a quiescent qāf and ḍamma on the sīn, is permissible. Whoever says "سُقُفًا" and "سُقْفًا" [takes it as] the plural of "سَقْف", as was said "رَهْن", "رُهُن" and "رُهْن"; and whoever says "سَقْفًا" [takes it as] a singular that indicates the plural, the meaning being: "We would have made for the house of each one of them a roof of silver".
And His saying: ﴿وَمَعارِجَ عَلَيْها يَظْهَرُونَ﴾ — "مَعارِج" are stairs; its singular is "مَعْرَج". The meaning is: "and We would have made stairs of silver"; and likewise ﴿أبْوابًا وسُرُرًا عَلَيْها يَتَّكِئُونَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 34], that is: doors of silver and couches of silver. ﴿وَزُخْرُفًا﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 35] — "الزُّخْرُف": it has come in the commentary that here it is gold, except for Zayd ibn Aslam, who said: it is the furnishings of the house. "الزُّخْرُف" in the language is ornament, and the perfection of a thing in it; the proof of that is His saying: ﴿حَتّى إذا أخَذَتِ الأرْضُ زُخْرُفَها﴾ [Yūnus: 24], that is: its perfection and completeness. ﴿وَإنْ كُلُّ ذَلِكَ لَمّا مَتاعُ الحَياةِ الدُّنْيا﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 35] — its meaning is: and all that is nothing but the enjoyment of the life of this world. And it is read "لَما مَتاعُ", and "ما" here is redundant (laghw); the meaning is: "لَمَتاعُ" (is surely the enjoyment).
And His saying: ﴿وَلَوْلا أنْ يَكُونَ النّاسُ أُمَّةً واحِدَةً﴾, that is: were it not that this world would sway them, so that all creatures would become disbelievers, Allah would give the disbeliever in this world the utmost of what he wishes for in it, because of how little it is in His sight; but He, Mighty and Majestic is He, did not do that, because of His knowledge that love of the immediate world prevails over creatures.

zajjaj:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿وَمَن يَعْشُ عَنْ ذِكْرِ الرَّحْمَنِ﴾ — and it is read "وَمَن يَعْشَ" with fatḥa on the shīn, from "عَشِيَ، يَعْشى", that is: "whoever is blind to the remembrance of the Most Merciful".
﴿نُقَيِّضْ لَهُ شَيْطانًا﴾: We assign to him a devil; Allah makes that his recompense.

zajjaj:37-37.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَحْسَبُونَ أنَّهم مُهْتَدُونَ﴾, that is: the devils turn them away from the path, and the disbelievers think that they are guided.
And His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمْ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33] — [لِبُيُوتِهِمْ] may be a badal (substitute) from His saying: ﴿لِمَن يَكْفُرُ بِالرَّحْمَنِ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 33], the meaning being: "We would have made for the houses of whoever disbelieves in the Most Merciful". And "لِبُيُوتِهِمْ" may be in the sense: "We would have made for whoever disbelieves in the Most Merciful, upon their houses".

zajjaj:4-4.t: His saying: ﴿وَإنَّهُ في أُمِّ الكِتابِ لَدَيْنا لَعَلِيٌّ حَكِيمٌ﴾ — "أُمُّ الكِتابِ" (the Mother of the Book) is the origin of the Book; the origin of everything is its mother. The Quran is recorded with Allah in the Preserved Tablet, and the proof of that is His saying: ﴿بَلْ هو قُرْآنٌ مَجِيدٌ﴾ [al-Burūj: 21] ﴿فِي لَوْحٍ مَحْفُوظٍ﴾ [al-Burūj: 22]

zajjaj:5-5.t: His saying: ﴿أفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ صَفْحًا أنْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا مُسْرِفِينَ﴾ — and it is read "إنْ كُنْتُمْ قَوْمًا مُسْرِفِينَ". Whoever gives it fatḥa, the meaning is: "Shall We then turn the Reminder away from you, disregarding you, because you are...?"; and whoever gives it kasra takes it in the sense of the future, in the sense: "if you are transgressors, We will turn the Reminder away from you". One says "ضَرَبْتُ عَنْهُ الذِّكْرَ" and "أضْرَبْتُ عَنْهُ الذِّكْرَ" (I turned the mention away from him). The meaning is: "Shall We then turn away from you the mention of punishment, and the punishment, because you have transgressed?!" The proof that the meaning is this, and that it is the mention of punishment, is His saying: ﴿فَأهْلَكْنا أشَدَّ مِنهم بَطْشًا ومَضى مَثَلُ الأوَّلِينَ﴾ [al-Zukhruf: 8], that is: their precedent has passed. "أفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكُمُ الذِّكْرَ" may also mean: "shall We neglect you and not make known to you what is obligatory upon you because you have transgressed"; and like it is: ﴿أيَحْسَبُ الإنْسانُ أنْ يُتْرَكَ سُدًى﴾ [al-Qiyāma: 36]
